rationale.complete: Round 1 done: predictions and nulls written before any real-data run, synthetic validation (two runs, 132 configurations on real call schedules), 32 replication periods plus 4 native tests (G31, G38, G51, NE42), channel attribution with in-cone controls, scorecard, and a guarded confirmatory script dry-run on stand-ins (not run). Round 2 must pre-register the matched jump and time-stamp the unlogged channel.
rationale.faithfulness: The logged light cone organizes the data where it binds: within-room adoptions almost never precede read-out (<= 4%, median 0.6%), 75-100% of cross-room adoptions fall outside the logged cone, and NE42's merge/split moves cross-group pickup 80-860x as predicted. But the pre-registered gating test failed (12/32); it passes (22/32) only with a post-hoc recency-matched estimator, about a third of fast adoptions look co-generated, the cadence and velocity predictions failed, and nothing is confirmed on the holdout.
rationale.usefulness: A computable diagnostic: logged chat explains almost no cross-room spread, and shared artifacts cannot be blamed from logs (they are as common in in-cone adoptions); human cross-posts are the only enriched leak. Rooms are strong cages for chat (merging multiplies cross-group pickup ~100x). Spread runs at about one hop per 1.5-5 talk turns, independent of call cadence. No validated control knob.

one_line: Inside rooms novel items follow a logged light cone (acausal <=4%); gating passed only post hoc (22/32); cross-room leaks bypass chat and can't be traced
